request.spec:
The sheet has a policy date (settings, SETTING_CHANGED key=policy-date value=<date>); when it is
blank the policy date is the sheet's today. A claim dated before the policy date rounds half up;
a claim dated on or after it rounds half to even. This decides every rounding of that claim's live
figures (the rate step and the late charge). A correction rounds by the date of the claim it
corrects, not its own. Settled figures stay frozen and figures bound by a statement stay bound.

agent.result_text:
The policy date now works, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What it does:** the sheet has a policy date setting. A claim dated before it rounds half up; a claim dated on or after it rounds half to even. When the setting is blank, the sheet's today is used. This rule applies to a claim's live rate step and its late charge. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects, not its own date. Settled dues and figures bound by a statement are stored values, so they don't change.

**Server**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V25__sheet_policy_date.sql`, adds a nullable `policy_date` column to the sheet.
- **Setting:** `PUT /settings/policy-date` saves it and writes `SETTING_CHANGED sheet=… by=… key=policy-date value=<date or blank>` to the audit file. Like the floor and late-percent saves, it runs inside `RollupService.track`, so any figures it moves are recorded in the audit too.
- **Rounding:** `ClaimService` now picks the rounding mode per claim, based on the date the claim rounds by (`roundsBy`). Before, it was always half to even.
- **Claim data sent to the screen:** each claim now carries its `roundsBy` date (the claim and statement endpoints work this out; quick-add claims are never corrections, so they use their own date).

**Front end**
- **Settings screen:** new `setting-policy-date` input and `setting-policy-date-current` display. Focusing the field counts as typing in it, so a blank value can be saved to clear the setting.
- **Second copy of the maths:** the screen calculates claim dues and person totals itself, separately from the server, and was hard-coded to half to even. My first test run failed because I had only changed the server. The screen now uses the same rule, comparing each claim's `roundsBy` with the policy date.

The screen and the server each keep their own copy of this rounding logic, so any future change to the rule has to be made in both places.
